scope: Current-table area and exact-tag audit for island food-system validation cases with explicit population or food-capacity intervals.

geometry_and_table_manifest.area_method: accepted-table land-area value derived from polynomial_coordinate_jacobian_v2+bounded_exact_crosswalks and the frozen coastal land contract; raw Jacobian area is retained for calibration diagnostics.

crosswalks.historical_boundary: Entire Rapa Nui (Easter Island), a single 164 km2 island.

eligibility.reason: Out-of-period/contact-era evidence and model-derived food scenarios do not establish an independently observed 1337 saturation fraction.

area_comparison.interpretation: Exact area agreement is an explicit frozen boundary calibration for this named island, not an uncalibrated polygon-intersection result. The raw Jacobian area is retained to prevent hiding the calibration.

historical_evidence.pressure_and_uncertainty: DiNapoli et al. fit radiocarbon demographic models and compare contact-era low-thousands populations with low- and high-bioavailable-nitrogen food scenarios. The 3,500 and 17,500 values are food-model scenarios, not independent saturation observations; Lima et al. revise rock-garden area and caution against treating the high scenario as a census.

current_model_diagnostic.scenario_comparison: The p50 is inside the wide 3,000-17,500 food-scenario envelope but above the independent contact-era population interval; retain this as a validation/uncertainty result, never as a training fit.

sources.citation: DiNapoli et al. (2021), Rapa Nui population history, Nature Communications 12:3939.
sources.locator: Abstract/Fig. 1 for 164 km2 island; Results/Table 1/Fig. 3 for demographic models and food-limited scenarios.

sources.citation: Lima et al. (2024), island-wide SWIR assessment of Rapa Nui rock gardens, Science Advances.
sources.locator: Island-wide rock-garden area and revised population-support interpretation.

crosswalks.resolution_method: The EU5 location_tag=rapa_nui is a single named island cell. The accepted table explicitly calibrates its land area to the published 164 km2 island boundary; model contributions and uncertainty were read from the same hash-pinned accepted row.
crosswalks.notes: This is the strongest exact-boundary validation fixture in the current Americas/Oceania set. It is not a 1337 scale anchor.

crosswalks.historical_boundary: Entire Tongatapu island, Kingdom of Tonga, published at approximately 260 km2.

eligibility.reason: The 18,000-24,000 capacity envelope is model-derived and conflicts with an independent 50,000-60,000 LiDAR reconstruction; dates and saturation semantics are not resolved for 1337 training.

area_comparison.interpretation: The selected island tag covers at least 96.86% of the published island land area under the frozen land mask. The raw Jacobian includes coastal/ocean footprint and is not used for population density.

historical_evidence.pressure_and_uncertainty: Archaeobotany/LiDAR documents forest removal, multicropping and local food investment. Green/Ussher-style capacity scenarios and the independent Parton/Clark LiDAR population reconstruction disagree by roughly a factor of three; preserve both and do not collapse them into one label.

current_model_diagnostic.scenario_comparison: The p50 is below the 18,000-24,000 capacity scenario but the p90 is near its upper bound; it is far below the independent 50,000-60,000 reconstruction. This is a useful uncertainty and island-area diagnostic, not a target.

sources.citation: Green and Ussher, Tongatapu local-food population/capacity reconstruction and island area.
sources.locator: Land-area, agricultural capacity and local-food reconstruction tables.

sources.citation: Parton and Clark (2022), LiDAR/Bayesian reconstruction of Tongan population, Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports.
sources.locator: Independent population reconstruction with materially higher interval; retained as a conflict diagnostic.

crosswalks.resolution_method: The EU5 location_tag=tongatapu is a single named island cell. The accepted land-area row is compared directly with the cited 260 km2 island area; no population is redistributed and no area multiplier is applied.
crosswalks.notes: High-coverage mapping qualifies this case for held-out validation, but not training because the independent historical intervals conflict and no defensible dated saturation fraction is available.

crosswalks.historical_boundary: Entire Mangareva island, with local food-system model area of 16.58 km2; the EU5 location tag is a much coarser Tuamotu footprint.

eligibility.reason: The coarse EU5 footprint is over eighteen times the published island area; no raw density or aggregate comparison is valid.

area_comparison.interpretation: The name tag is semantically useful but not area-coextensive. Coverage is intentionally null rather than falsely reported as 1.0.

historical_evidence.pressure_and_uncertainty: Puleston et al. provide GIS food-budget scenarios for terraced horticulture, arboriculture, marine/lagoon resources and labour constraints, but no independent dated saturation interval.

current_model_diagnostic.scenario_comparison: Because the EU5 footprint is non-coextensive, the 16,041-person p50 is not compared to the 2,954-5,139 island scenario as a quantitative error. The mismatch is retained as a mapping failure.

sources.citation: Puleston et al. (2024), GIS reconstruction of Mangareva food-system capacity.
sources.locator: GIS area and food-budget scenario tables.

crosswalks.resolution_method: The exact EU5 name tag was matched, but current calibrated land area was compared against the source island area and failed coextensive-area validation. No population or capacity is redistributed to the coarse footprint.
crosswalks.notes: Retain as a negative control for area handling and marine/crop decomposition; it must not train or set scale.

summary.key_result: Rapa Nui is an exact named-island validation fixture after explicit area calibration; Tongatapu is a 96.86% high-coverage island fixture with unresolved historical interval conflict; Mangareva remains a deliberate non-coextensive negative control.
summary.required_follow_up: Keep all three out of training. Use them in generalization and physical-invariant reports, and only reconsider Tongatapu if the conflicting population reconstructions and saturation semantics are independently reconciled.
